identity.name: Ammonia caramel
identity.chemical_class: Class III caramel colour produced via ammonia process; complex process-derived caramelization products

function.mechanism: Controlled heat treatment of carbohydrates (with permitted acids/alkalis/salts including ammonium reagents) forms brown chromophoric polymers that impart color.

adi.basis: EFSA group ADI for caramel colours E150a, E150b, E150c and E150d.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA retained a group ADI of 300 mg/kg bw/day (2011 re-evaluation), with 2012 refined exposure indicating mean exposures below ADI but possible conservative high-end exceedance in some children/toddlers.

adi.basis: JECFA Class III caramel entry lists ADI 0-200 mg/kg bw (comment: 0-150 mg/kg bw on a solids basis).

concerns.summary: No direct IARC classification for E150c was identified, but related process contaminant 4-methylimidazole (4-MEI) is listed by IARC as Group 2B.
A 2024 mouse study reported immunotoxic effects for THI (a Class III caramel by-product), including reduced lymphocyte-related endpoints and higher sensitivity in vitamin B6-deficient mice.

A 2025 cohort study linked one food-additive mixture including sulphite ammonia caramel (E150d) with higher type 2 diabetes incidence, but evidence is observational and mixture-level, not specific causal evidence for E150c.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA continues to authorize caramel colours with a defined group ADI.
FDA Title 21 permits caramel as a color additive under GMP and lists caramel as GRAS under GMP.
JECFA lists Class III caramel ADI at 0-200 mg/kg bw.
Recent U.S. 4-MEI exposure reassessment indicates lower estimated exposure than earlier estimates.

populations: toddlers (high consumers in conservative EFSA scenarios)
children (high consumers in conservative EFSA scenarios)
adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA exceedance concern is based on grouped caramel colours (E150a-d), not an E150c-only exposure model.

risk_assessment.rationale: E150c remains approved across major regulators, but moderate concern is warranted due to ADI-managed status, modeled high-end pediatric exceedance risk in EFSA group exposure scenarios, and toxicological concern for Class III-related by-products (THI and 4-MEI).
key_factors: EFSA group ADI 300 mg/kg bw/day for E150a-d
EFSA 2012 refined exposure still showing conservative high-end pediatric exceedance potential
FDA authorization under 21 CFR 73.85 and GRAS listing for caramel under 21 CFR 182.1235
JECFA ADI 0-200 mg/kg bw for Class III caramel
IARC Group 2B listing for related contaminant 4-MEI, but no direct E150c IARC classification
